result:
I tested 8 properties of `setuptools.package_index` and found two real bugs. Six properties passed.

### Bug 1: downloads can be written outside `tmpdir` (High, Logic)
`bug_report_setuptools_package_index_2026-10-28_18-18_8o5k.md`

The `download()` docstring promises that a URL "is downloaded to a subpath of `tmpdir`". It doesn't hold. `_resolve_download_filename` decodes `%2F` in the last part of the URL path into a real `/` before joining it onto `tmpdir`. An absolute path then replaces `tmpdir` entirely:

```
https://example.com/%2Fetc%2Fpasswd  ->  /etc/passwd
https://example.com/sub%2Fx.tar.gz   ->  /tmp/dl/sub/x.tar.gz
```

So a malicious index page or `--find-links` URL can overwrite any file the user can write to. This is CVE-2025-47273, which this checkout is named after. Hypothesis shrank it to the URL `https://example.com/%2F`, which resolves to `/`. The report includes the upstream-style patch: reject any filename that doesn't start with `tmpdir`. I didn't run that patch.

### Bug 2: the `REL` regex takes cubic time on untrusted HTML (Medium)
`bug_report_setuptools_package_index_2026-10-28_18-18_yhtm.md`

`find_external_links` runs on every package page fetched over the network. On a page of repeated `< rel=` with no closing `>`, it slows down about 8× each time the input doubles:

| Page size | Time |
|---|---|
| 3 KB | 0.6 s |
| 6 KB | 4.6 s |
| 12 KB | 37 s |
| 18 KB | 123 s |

A few kilobytes of hostile HTML can hang an install. The fix in the report splits the page on `>` and looks for `rel=` inside each piece. A Hypothesis test over 3000 random pages showed it returns exactly the same matches as the old regex, and it handles 120 KB of the attack input in under a millisecond. That check is in `fix_check.py`.

### What passed
- Ordinary file names are kept unchanged.
- `_encode_auth` round-trips through base64 and never adds a newline.
- `htmldecode(html.escape(s)) == s`.
- `parse_bdist_wininst` handles all four `.exe` name forms.
- `_vcs_split_rev_from_url` splits a VCS URL into clean URL and revision.
- `interpret_distro_name` splits the name from the version at the first part that starts with a digit.

**Two things to know about the test files:**
- `test_no_regex_blowup[page6]` in `test_pkgindex.py` takes about two minutes and then fails. That is the bug showing, not a broken test.
- I excluded a URL whose last segment is just `.` from the path test. It resolves to `tmpdir` itself, which isn't an escape.

The claims are in `claims.md` and the tests in `test_pkgindex.py`.
